title: The Alpha and Epsilon Structural Levels
deck: The Alpha and Epsilon Levels begin the six-level structural hierarchy: Merons constitute the Alpha Level, while stars constitute the Epsilon Level.

concise.body:
The Alpha and Epsilon Structural Levels

The Alpha and Epsilon Levels are the first two structural levels in the hierarchy extending from Merons to the largest cosmic organizations.

Alpha Level, the First Structural Level

The Alpha Level is formed by the infinitely many existing Merons acting as basic functional units throughout the spatially infinite universe—the Omega Dimension.

Its dimensional range extends from the simplest Meron and molecular aggregates to the largest Meronic bodies. All are constituted of Merons acting as basic building blocks.

Figure 06.2.1 — Merons, the constituent elements of the Alpha Level.

Epsilon Level, the Second Structural Level

The Epsilon Level is composed of the infinitely many stars acting as basic functional units throughout the Omega Dimension.

Stars in their various forms—including pulsars, quasars, and magnetars—act as the basic building blocks of galaxies.

Figure 06.2.2 — Stars, the constituent elements of the Epsilon Level.

full.body:
The Alpha and Epsilon Structural Levels

The Alpha and Epsilon levels are the first two levels of structures ranging from Merons to Stars.

Alpha Level, the First Structural Level

The Alpha Level is formed by all the infinitely many existing Merons (atoms) acting as basic functional units distributed throughout the spatially infinite universe—that is, the infinite Omega Dimension.

The functional elements falling within the Alpha Level's dimensional range span from the scale of the "smallest" and simplest Meron (the Metalpha)—including molecules and molecular aggregates the size of dust grains—up to the scale of the largest existing stars. All these elements serve as basic functional units; that is, each element acts as an autonomous organism immersed in a sea of organisms of the same nature.

All bodies within this dimensional range are, so to speak, merely small or large Meronic aggregates, whether or not they possess a system of other orbiting aggregates (bodies). They are all constituted of Merons acting as basic building blocks, and all belong to the same dimensional range.

Figure 06.2.1 — Merons, the constituent elements of the Alpha Level

Epsilon Level, the Second Structural Level

The Epsilon Level is composed of all the infinite stars that exist, which act as basic functional units distributed throughout the universal fullness—that is, the infinite Omega Dimension.

The functional elements that fall within the Dimensional Range of the Epsilon Level are those with Structural Dimensions ranging from the smallest to the largest existing stars, in their various forms—that is, as pulsars, quasars, magnetars, etc. These structures, as the basic functional cells, form galaxies, since every existing galaxy is composed of a functional cluster of stars and other smaller bodies, acting as Basic Building Blocks.

Figure 06.2.2 — Stars, the constituent elements of the Epsilon Level.
